body:
@feross Thanks for the issue! If you're reporting a bug, please be sure to include:
1. The version of ESLint you are using (run `eslint -v`)
2. What you did (the source code and ESLint configuration)
3. The actual ESLint output complete with numbers
4. What you expected to happen instead

Requesting a new rule? Please see [Proposing a New Rule](http://eslint.org/docs/developer-guide/contributing/new-rules) for instructions.

The object passed to `CLIEngine` is not an ESLint config object, so it doesn't have the same fields.
- There's no such thing as `extends` on the CLI because there's no configuration to extend. You can use `configFile` to specify the same value as `-c` on the CLI or `baseConfig` to specify the base config to use, including `extends`.
- It looks like `plugins` is present. When you say "it's missing," what does that mean? Are you seeing an error? Is something not working as expected?

> There's no such thing as `extends` on the CLI

Okay, fair enough. Though this means that it's not possible to invoke the CLI directly on a shared configuration without creating an extra file on the filesystem and referencing that with `-c`. I expected this to work:

```
npm install eslint eslint-config-standard
eslint --extends standard test.js
```
`plugins` is missing from the [Node JS API documentation](http://eslint.org/docs/2.0.0/developer-guide/nodejs-api) for v2.0.0.
@feross I don't think `CLIEngine` supports plugins directly. You should use [addPlugin](http://eslint.org/docs/2.0.0/developer-guide/nodejs-api#addplugin) method instead.

@ilyavolodin Related, it seems pointless that `CLIEngine` excepts those plugins on its constructor but that it doesn't actually do anything unless you call `engine.addPlugin()`. Any reason why that option is even on the constructor in the first place?

I don't think it's in the constructor. Constructor takes baseConfig, which is config object that can accept `plugins` among other things (or at least under regular conditions it can). Problem is, since `baseConfig` isn't processed by config-file, plugins will not be loaded. But documentation doesn't specify that you can supply `plugins` as part of `baseConfig` and have them be loaded (however, it doesn't specify otherwise either, so that might need to be fixed).

It is accepted as part of the constructor options. So you can do:

``` js
var engine = new CLIEngine({ plugins: ["foo"] });
```

Those get passed through to [Config](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/master/lib/cli-engine.js#L492), which uses it to [load plugins](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/master/lib/config.js#L254).

So, looks like it's just missing from the docs but actually does work.

I'm not sure it does. I had to call addPlugin to make my plugin's
integration tests work. But this issue has gone off track, so I will open a
new issue if I can reproduce again.
On Feb 9, 2016 1:16 PM, "Nicholas C. Zakas" notifications@github.com
wrote:

This only affects master, not any stable releases.

It should fix the main problem in #1806 although we still shouldn't close the issue until we fix the end-to-end tests and make eject crash on error.

I'd appreciate the review because I haven't really tested it. We can look at Travis logs to verify it worked.

I want to merge this sooner than other issues in #1806 so that less forkers who track master are affected.
